review_text_raw: After waiting so long I finally got around to playing this and I can say, the reviews I saw when this first released lied to me. This game released 3 years ago and I never saw anyone play it or talk about it. After playing it for myself, I can see why.

Honestly, the biggest compliment i can give this game is "It's alright." The game still has an interesting mystery to solve like the other ones do but for some reason they really went off the horror with this one. I feel like what made the first Simulacra so good wasn't just the investigating a phone gameplay, it was the horror aspect of it. The jumpscares were good and it genuinely made you uncomfortable with other little details that really added to the experience, and I would say even Pipe Dreams and 2 got this right, but this one was just not scary at all. There was one jumpscare at most and even then it wasn't a good one. 

If you liked the other Simulacra games for how they made you use your brain to work things out, you might like this game? But if like me, you are looking for decent horror, you should just skip this one because there is absolutely none of it here.

review_text_raw:
Simulacra 3, developed by Kaigan Games and published by Neon Doctrine, continues the found-phone horror tradition established by its predecessors, delivering an immersive narrative experience centered around digital mystery and psychological suspense. Set in the eerie town of Stonecreek, the game places players in the role of an intern at a local newspaper tasked with assisting investigative journalist Ruby Myers. The central mystery revolves around the disappearance of Paul Castillo, a software developer whose phone becomes the gateway to unraveling the secrets behind his vanishing. By exploring his digital life through texts, photos, videos, and various apps, players are drawn into a chilling tale that combines supernatural elements with a realistic portrayal of modern technology, creating a sense of intimacy and urgency that few horror games achieve.

The gameplay is built around interacting with Paul's smartphone, where every notification, message, and multimedia file serves as a piece of the puzzle. Players navigate through different apps, decode cryptic information, and use hacking mechanics to access deeper layers of the mystery. The real-time progression of events adds tension and immediacy, encouraging quick decisions that influence the unfolding story. This dynamic storytelling approach allows multiple branching endings based on player choices, enhancing replay value and inviting players to revisit the narrative to uncover all possible outcomes. The interface cleverly mimics a real phone’s UI, making the experience feel personal and immersive, as if players are genuinely investigating a missing person’s digital footprint.

Visually, Simulacra 3 stays true to the series' minimalist yet effective design, presenting a realistic smartphone interface filled with authentic-looking apps and multimedia content. The integration of live-action video calls and interactive elements boosts immersion, while the sound design subtly heightens the suspense throughout the investigation. Despite these strengths, some players have found certain puzzles to be ambiguous or overly obscure, which can stall progression and disrupt the narrative flow. The pacing, while deliberately methodical to build atmosphere, may feel slow to those expecting more traditional horror gameplay or quicker resolutions.

Critical reception for Simulacra 3 has been varied, reflecting its niche appeal. While some reviewers praise its atmospheric storytelling, innovative use of the found-phone format, and the effective blend of horror with investigative mechanics, others point out shortcomings in character depth and the occasional frustration with puzzle design. The player community echoes this division, with many appreciating the eerie mood and unique narrative delivery but expressing disappointment over certain gameplay limitations and the game's pacing. For fans of narrative-driven horror and those intrigued by the concept of piecing together stories through digital clues, Simulacra 3 offers a compelling experience, though it may not resonate with everyone.

In summary, Simulacra 3 represents a strong continuation of the found-phone horror genre, delivering a haunting and interactive story that makes clever use of modern technology as a storytelling device. Its immersive atmosphere and branching narrative paths offer a deep dive into mystery and supernatural horror, appealing especially to players who enjoy investigative and choice-driven games. While some gameplay elements and pacing choices might divide opinion, the game stands as a noteworthy title for those looking to explore a psychologically tense and digitally immersive horror experience.

Rating: 6/10

This game in its entirety is 'decent' at best. I like the SIMULACRA games, but I feel like this one was rushed. Cutscenes and acting look and sound worse compared to the other games in the series. Only like 2 jumpscares throughout the ENTIRE game. I had high expectations when playing this game and it was just disappointing. I would recommend this game just for the story, cause it was actually pretty good and its probably the only thing that redeems itself compared to the rest of the game. Yes it's short but it's better than Simulacra 1 and Simulacra: Pipe Dreams.

review_text_raw:
[h1] THE GOOD: [/h1]
-Acting is great all around. It's been a trip seeing this series go from "F**K YOU SOOOO MUUUUCCCCCHHHH!" to what we have now.
-A fantastic story with fun twists on the endings for how the SIMULACRA can be handled.
-UI and interface is snappy and I never had a hard time navigating around.
-Puzzles are mostly great, with only a few that might hold you up towards the end (One in particular needs you to verify by the month when certain people went missing, which might take you a while if you haven't been paying attention to where they are in each of the apps)

[h1] THE BAD: [/h1]
-Compared to the first two games (And Pipe Dreams if you like to include that), there is a lot more emphasis on chatting and a lot less focus on scares. This isn't something that particularly bothered me, but I do understand why a lot of people feel negatively about it considering how well known the series is for its balance of scares.
-Speaking of scares, there's exactly one jumpscare in this entire game outside of a couple of fail states. Even the usual background ambiance in 1 and 2 that's meant to throw you off (Like if you're wearing headphones) isn't as pronounced here, and I wish the game had more of it.
-While the cast is all around great, most of your time with them is spent texting. There's a lot less FMV and voice acting goodness this time around, but part of that is due to a mechanic later on that more than likely ate up most of the production budget.

[h1] OVERALL: [/h1]

I stayed away for a long time due to its 'Mixed' reviews, and I kind of wish I didn't. It's certainly weaker than the first two in terms of scares and the sheer amount of reading you do, but its story is pretty strong and it doesn't overstay its welcome. If you're looking for a more horror focused entry in this series I'd certainly stick to 1 and 2, but this is an easy recommend for me to play in an afternoon and get invested in the happenings of Stonecreek and its citizens. If you're unsure if you'd like it, I'd definitely recommend waiting on a sale.

[h1] RECOMMENDATION SCALE: [/h1]
-BUY IT
[h2]-WAIT FOR SALE/PATCHES [/h2]
-IGNORE IT

review_text_raw:
I liked it, it's an ok - good game according to my taste and if you played any other games in the Simulacra Franchise (like Simulacra 1/2 or Simulacra - Pipe Dreams [free]) or from the Kaigan Games Devs from Malaysia (like their Dr. Who lost Phone investigation game) and liked them, you'll probably enjoy this one, too (can play them in any order you want, as the stories are isolated and not dependent on each other save for a few minor easter eggs and references, etc.)

It's far from perfect though, my biggest criticism would probably be the drove of spelling mistakes in the English language version. It appears as if the later development has been rushed or the translators were on crunch time and there wasn't a single proof reading or QA-testing for the English language version at least, which just baffles my mind.

Has some nice achievements at least but the sped up version for further play troughs from the earlier games is missing.
Also has a little replayability, but there are a lot less choices / different paths & options you can take than the seocnd game still had.

if you liked this, maybe check out Kaigan Games other games if you haven't played them yet:
Sarah is missing, Simulacra (1), Simulacra: Pipe Dreams (free to play and good intro to see if you'd like this paid one, too), Simulacra 2 and maybe Doctor Who: The Lonely Assassins, which is a similar Lost phone / investigative mystery game.

A conflicted thumbs up. This is a weaker title than Simulacra 2, and that's something you should know walking into this.

Is it a neat game? Yeah. Did I enjoy it? Yeah. But it... this game has all the pieces to multiple different really excellent stories, but... they just didn't come together very well. My wife and were theory crafting all the way through and we had a lot of moments where 'What if the game did ____ That would be so awesome!' And then the awesome thing never happened. The game get a flat C from me, if you're curious about the games and styles, take the first or the second one before this, they're both just better stories to play through.

Cheers to the devs, hope they make more games, and continue to grow.
